info.name: OpenWA Bridge
info.description:
Send WhatsApp messages and read the MongoDB archive.

Set the collection variables `baseUrl` (http://localhost:8000, or this machine's address from another PC) and `apiKey` (BRIDGE_API_KEY from bridge/.env) first.

variable.description: The bridge URL. http://localhost:8000 on this machine.
BRIDGE_API_KEY from .env at the project root - sent as Authorization: Bearer

request.description:
One endpoint for every chat - the recipient is `id` in the body, not a per-chat URL.

`id` is the phone number including the country code (no + or spaces required), or a group id like 120363...@g.us.
`msg` is the text, up to 4096 characters.

To send a file instead, see the two requests below.

Auth is the collection-level Bearer token. Returns the WhatsApp message id, which is also the key of the MongoDB document.

Send a file that is already hosted somewhere. The gateway fetches the URL itself, so nothing large travels through the bridge and there is no upload size limit to worry about.

`media` also accepts a data: URI or raw base64.

The kind of WhatsApp message is chosen from the mimetype - image/* becomes a photo, video/* a video, audio/* an audio message, anything else a document. Set `type` to override it: image, video, audio, voice, document or sticker. `voice` sends audio as a voice note (the mic bubble with a waveform).

`msg` becomes the caption here, and WhatsApp caps captions at 1024 characters.

Note: URL sends are not copied to data/media - the bytes never pass through the bridge. mediaInfo.sourceUrl records where it came from.

Send a file from this machine. Pick it in the `file` row - Postman sets the Content-Type header itself, so leave that alone.

The file's own type decides how it arrives; add a `type` field to override.

Uploads ARE archived: the bridge holds the bytes, so it writes a copy under data/media/ and returns the path as `mediaPath`.

About 24 MiB is the ceiling, measured after base64 encoding. Larger than that, host the file and use the URL request instead.
No auth required. `ok` is true only when MongoDB is reachable, OpenWA is reachable, and the WhatsApp session is `ready`.
Newest first, straight out of MongoDB. Filter by `direction` (in/out) or `chatId`.
The WhatsApp session's state: created / initializing / qr_ready / authenticating / ready / disconnected.
Returns `qrCode` as a PNG data URL. Paste it into a browser address bar to view and scan it.

Recreates the WhatsApp session and the gateway's event subscription. Only needed if the bridge started before the gateway, or the subscription was deleted in the dashboard. This is internal plumbing - not your WEBHOOK_URL.
